title: What he left
hook: no palace, no wealth, the Qur'an and his way

segments.voice: Yesterday, Abu Bakr's words: whoever worshiped Muhammad, he has died; whoever worships God, al-Hayy, God is alive and does not die. Your line was allah is alive and does not die. What felt steady underneath? Day two hundred ninety-two.
screen: `ALLAH IS ALIVE AND DOES NOT DIE.`

segments.voice: When a powerful person dies, there's usually an inventory. The houses, the accounts, the paintings, the lawyers arguing about who gets what. By the end of his life, delegations had crossed Arabia to reach the Prophet ﷺ, bringing gifts. So what was in his estate? A companion named 'Amr ibn al-Harith answered that question, and al-Bukhari recorded it. Aisha added a detail about his armor. Today, the inventory, and our word.
screen: `THE INVENTORY.` → `DELEGATIONS BROUGHT GIFTS.` → `SO WHAT DID HE LEAVE?`

segments.voice: 'Amr said: he left no gold coin and no silver coin, no servants, nothing, except his white mule, his weapons, and a piece of land he had given away as charity. And Aisha said that when he died, his armor was held by a Jewish man in Medina, pawned as security for some barley. The man delegations crossed Arabia to meet died owing a neighbor for grain. But he did leave something. A hadith says prophets don't leave gold or silver behind; they leave knowledge, and whoever takes it takes a great share. He left the Qur'an, and he left his way. That's our word: sunnah. It means a way, a well-trodden path, an established custom. The sunnah is how he prayed, how he ate, how he treated his wives and children and animals, how he forgave, how he mended his own shoes. The hadith are the reports that carry it; the sunnah is the way itself. Muslims hold to it alongside the Qur'an. A report in Sahih Muslim also speaks of the Book of God and his family, the ahl al-bayt. Shia Muslims give that report special weight and receive the sunnah through the Prophet's family; Sunni Muslims, whose very name comes from sunnah, hold the family in honor too. And that closes this stretch of the path. Since Quba, we've walked through Medina with him: a mosque of palm trunks, brothers by choice, Badr and Uhud and the Trench, home life and the children and the animals, Hudaybiyyah and Mecca, the farewell, the small room. No palace at the end. Just a way, trodden enough for others to walk.
screen: `A MULE, HIS WEAPONS, LAND GIVEN AWAY.` · `ARMOR PAWNED FOR BARLEY.` · `SUNNAH — A WELL-TRODDEN WAY.` · `FROM QUBA TO THE SMALL ROOM.` · then, large: `HE LEFT THE WAY.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: give something away. Sit, and breathe. Picture the room you live in, and everything in it. Now pick one thing you don't need, something with some worth, a coat, a book, a tool, some money, and decide who it will go to. Hold that decision for a moment. Notice whether your hand wants to close around it. After the bell, give it. If you pray, you can ask that what you leave behind be a way and not a pile. The bell holds the time.
Sunnah. The Prophet's way, a well-trodden path, carried in the hadith and followed alongside the Qur'an. Today's word.
Your line: he left the way. Today, give one thing away, and do one small thing the way you'd want someone to learn it from you. Day two hundred ninety-two.

howItsDone: Muslims follow the sunnah alongside the Qur'an, learning the Prophet's way through the hadith collections, in matters from prayer and fasting to eating, greeting and treating family and neighbors.

original.note: Arabic: a way, a custom, a well-trodden path. the Prophet's way, followed alongside the Qur'an.

trapdoor: what it means: the Prophet's way of living, a well-trodden path, carried in the hadith and walked alongside the Qur'an.
what a scholar hears: sunnah first meant any established custom; the reports of his estate (al-Bukhari 2739, 2916) show he left a way, not wealth.

Editor review (2026-10-01): cut 'leader of most of Arabia' and 'the most powerful man in Arabia' (unsourced superlative), stock 'stops people short', and the unsourced 'the gifts had gone to others'; 'a path worn smooth by walking' was a preacher's etymology, now 'a way, a well-trodden path, an established custom' (Lane); the Shia line now says Shia Muslims also follow the sunnah, received through the ahl al-bayt.
